title: Personality and eating disorders
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's personality or eating disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for weight loss and eating habits.

Vitals: BP 118/76, HR 74, Temp 98.6 F, SpO2 98% on room air, Height 5'10", Weight 135 lbs.

Recent Labs: BMI: 19.5. Electrolytes: Sodium 139, Potassium 4.0, Chloride 102, CO2 24. BUN 12, Creatinine 0.8. Glucose 92.

Social History: Patient is a 51-year-old male employed full-time. He lives with his spouse and two children. He reports no tobacco use and denies recreational drug use.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes. No family history of similar eating disorders.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, fatigue.
Neurological: Negative for dizziness, syncope.
Cardiovascular: Negative for palpitations, chest pain.
Respiratory: Negative for shortness of breath.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for nausea, constipation.
Musculoskeletal: Negative for joint pain.
Psychiatric: Negative for hallucinations.

HPI: (Copied Forward) Patient is a 51-year-old male presenting for management of anorexia nervosa. He reports a significant decrease in caloric intake over the last six months, primarily driven by an intense fear of weight gain. He describes a strict regimen of calorie counting and avoidance of fats. He has been struggling to maintain a healthy weight and reports feelings of anxiety regarding his body image. He is currently working with a support team to address these behaviors.

Exam: Patient appears well-nourished but thin. Alert and oriented x3. Speech is clear. No tremors noted. Heart rate is regular. Lungs are clear to auscultation. Abdomen is soft, non-tender. No significant muscle wasting noted.

Assessment: 
1. Anorexia nervosa, restricting type, moderate severity.

Plan:
1. Continue current treatment plan for anorexia nervosa.
2. Patient will continue to attend weekly sessions with a registered dietitian to establish a structured meal plan.
3. Patient will continue weekly sessions with a therapist to address the psychological components of his restricting type behavior.
4. Monitor weight at each follow-up visit.
5. Return to clinic in four weeks for progress evaluation.

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Anorexia nervosa, restricting type, moderate: F50.011 (HCC 153).

distractors.why: The type and severity are documented.
The restricting type is documented, not binge-purge.
